section_title: What does the risen Christ reveal about His care and authority?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 12 Then I turned to see the voice that was speaking with me. And having turned, I saw seven golden lampstands, 13 and among the lampstands was One like the Son of Man, dressed in a long robe, with a golden sash around His chest. 14 The hair of His head was white like wool, as white as snow, and His eyes were like a blazing fire. 15 His feet were like polished bronze refined in a furnace, and His voice was like the roar of many waters. 16 He held in His right hand seven stars, and a sharp double-edged sword came from His mouth. His face was like the sun shining at its brightest.

17 When I saw Him, I fell at His feet like a dead man. But He placed His right hand on me and said, “Do not be afraid. I am the First and the Last, 18 the Living One. I was dead, and behold, now I am alive forever and ever! And I hold the keys of Death and of Hades.

19 Therefore write down the things you have seen, the things that are, and the things that will happen after this. 20 This is the mystery of the seven stars you saw in My right hand and of the seven golden lampstands: The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and the seven lampstands are the seven churches.

context_lines: John turns and sees seven golden lampstands and One like the Son of Man among them. The robe, golden sash, white hair, fiery eyes, bronze-like feet and powerful voice present a vision of majesty and authority.

The language recalls earlier visions. [Daniel 7:9–14](https://biblehub.com/bsb/daniel/7.htm) describes the Ancient of Days with white hair and the Son of Man receiving dominion. [Daniel 10:4–12](https://biblehub.com/bsb/daniel/10.htm) includes a golden belt, fiery eyes, shining limbs and an overwhelming voice. These are connections between the descriptions; they do not require every detail in the two earlier visions to have one identical meaning.

John falls as though dead, but the speaker touches him and tells him not to fear. He identifies Himself as the First and the Last, the Living One who died and now lives forever. His authority extends to Death and Hades, the realm of the dead.

He commands John to write, then explains two features of the vision: the stars are the angels of the seven churches and the lampstands are the churches themselves. The opening vision therefore places the living Christ among His churches and shows them held within His care and authority.
common_interpretation_lines: [Wesley](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-revelation-of-jesus-christ/) and the [USCCB notes](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/revelation/1) read the description as a portrayal of Christ’s divine majesty, with royal and priestly features. Wesley explicitly distinguishes the vision’s symbolic appearance from a complete description of how Christ appears in heaven. Both find reassurance in His victory over death.

The angels of the churches receive different explanations. Wesley understands each as the church’s pastor or ruling minister. The USCCB note favors heavenly spirits connected with the churches, while also recording the possibilities of a pastor or a symbol for the congregation itself. Verse 20 identifies the stars as angels, but does not itself explain which of those senses is intended.
god_plan_lines: [Hebrews 2:14–18](https://biblehub.com/bsb/hebrews/2.htm) explains that Christ shared human life and passed through death to free people from slavery to its fear. The One who tells John not to fear is that same crucified and living Savior. His majesty and His care belong together: His victory over death serves the people He came to save.
